posts.text: Ola Electric launches S1Z scooter with Bharat Cell LFP, starting at ₹79,999 – deliveries from Dec 2026 S1Z scooter launched with Bharat Cell LFP technology 3.1 kWh variant: ₹ 79,999, range up to 179 kms (IDC) 5.1 kWh variant: ₹ 99,999, range up to 301 kms (IDC) Deliveries: 3.1 kWh from Dec 2026, 5.1 kWh from March 2027 The Ola S1Z will be the first product range to ramp up through Ola Electric’s next phase of retail expansion through its first dealer-operated stores, beyond a company-owned retail network. This is set to significantly expand access to Ola products across the country.

posts.author: dpk1994
posts.community: Ola Electric - Full Stack EV play?
posts.text: The EV transition and BESS are the reality, and this shift is likely to accelerate faster than most currently expect. Ola is going through a struggling period, which is common among new-age companies, especially those still in the nascent stage of their lifecycle. This by no means suggests that the story is over for Ola. You’ll find ample examples of companies that continuously adjust their strategies until they find what works. The real risk lies in being complacent about the status quo and failing to stay agile. The recent shift to a dealership model is one such instance where Ola recognized…

posts.author: dpk1994
posts.community: Ola Electric - Full Stack EV play?
posts.text: Mahashakti is expected to be based on prismatic LFP battery which is still under development. R&D is expected to be completed by Dec 2026. So he maybe right in a sense that Ola announced MoU before Prismatic cells are ready. I would also advise caution against such blogs as they are often based on individual limited research and knowledge. MoUs are an indicator of product acceptance in the market and also act as an anchor customer. For example if a company is building a chemical plant they will get some anchor customers who will Commit to the portion of installed capacity even before the plant…
